cases.description: Microsoft's documented worked example: inverse hyperbolic cotangent of 6
cases.expected_note: Microsoft's page publishes this example's result as 0.168. Independently verified from the documented identity acoth(x) = 0.5*ln((x+1)/(x-1)) = atanh(1/x): atanh(1/6) = 0.16823611831060645 -> 0.168 at 3 dp

cases.description: A negative argument whose absolute value exceeds 1, which the documented domain allows
cases.expected_note: Excel documents "The absolute value of Number must be greater than 1", so -2 is in the domain. Independently derived from 0.5*ln((x+1)/(x-1)) with x = -2: 0.5*ln(1/3) = -0.5493061443340548 -> -0.549306144 at 9 dp

cases.description: An argument whose absolute value is below 1 is outside the documented domain
cases.expected_note: Excel documents: "If Number is less than 1, ACOTH returns the #NUM! error value." (The page's next line repeats the rule for the absolute value but misnames the function as ACOT and misnames the error as #VALUE!; the #NUM! statement is the one that names ACOTH, and 0.5 satisfies both stated conditions)
#VALUE! is Excel's documented error for an argument of the wrong type; the companion ACOT page states it explicitly for this function family
